questions.question: Which description fits the **CarePlan** resource?
options: Describes the intention of how one or more practitioners intend to deliver care for a particular patient, group or community for a period of time, possibly limited to care for a specific condition or set of conditions.
A request to supply a diet, formula feeding (enteral) or oral nutritional supplement to a patient/resident.
A record of a request for service such as diagnostic investigations, treatments, or operations to be performed.
An assessment of the likely outcome(s) for a patient or other subject as well as the likelihood of each outcome.
questions.explanation: **CarePlan**: Describes the intention of how one or more practitioners intend to deliver care for a particular patient, group or community for a period of time, possibly limited to care for a specific condition or set of conditions. The other descriptions belong to **NutritionOrder**, **ServiceRequest**, **RiskAssessment**.

questions.question: Which resource would you use? The plan for managing a patient’s heart failure, with planned activities and goals.
questions.explanation: **CarePlan**. How care will be delivered for a condition over time.

questions.question: You know **CarePlan**. Which resource should you use instead when you need “one target outcome”?
questions.explanation: **Goal**: one target outcome. **CarePlan** is for something else: Describes the intention of how one or more practitioners intend to deliver care for a particular patient, group or community for a period of time, possibly limited to care for a specific condition or set of conditions.

questions.question: Which element is **required** (minimum cardinality 1) in every **CarePlan** instance?
questions.explanation: The required top-level elements of CarePlan are `status` (1..1), `intent` (1..1), `subject` (1..1). The other options have a minimum cardinality of 0, so they are optional.

questions.question: Which element of **CarePlan** is a **modifier** (?!), so receiving systems must not ignore it?
questions.explanation: Modifier elements of CarePlan: `status`, `intent`. `status`: draft | active | on-hold | revoked | completed | entered-in-error | unknown. A modifier can change the meaning of the whole resource: for example, a status of `entered-in-error` means the data must not be used.
